pages.title: The pause
pages.body: Silence is a tool. Using pauses helps your audience digest information and makes your most important points feel more significant.
pages.learn: Use silence, not "um," to make your key line land.

steps.label: Pick your line
steps.text: Identify the most important point you want to communicate.

steps.label: Pause before
steps.text: Stop for a beat to create meaning and capture attention.

steps.label: Speak slowly
steps.text: Slowing your rate helps the point come across as important.

steps.label: Pause after
steps.text: Give the audience time to absorb and process the information.

steps.label: Stay silent
steps.text: When you need to think, use silence instead of filler sounds.

pages.title: Before and after
pages.situation: Telling a coworker about a project deadline.
pages.before: The deadline is, um, tomorrow, so we should probably, like, finish the slides tonight.
pages.after: The deadline is... (pause) tomorrow. (pause) We need to finish the slides tonight.
pages.why: It replaces distracting fillers with a deliberate pace.

pages.title: Why it works
pages.body: Controlled pauses prevent the audience from becoming distracted and give them the necessary time to mentally digest your words.

cite.book: Exploring Public Speaking, 4th ed. (Tucker et al.)

quiz.q: You have identified your most important point. How should you deliver it to maximize impact?
options: Speak quickly to keep the energy high
Pause before, speak slowly, then pause after
Pause only after the point is finished
quiz.explain: This sequence creates attention, emphasizes the point, and allows for digestion.

quiz.q: You forget your next word while speaking. What is the best way to handle this gap?
options: Use a filler sound like 'um' to keep flow
Speed up your pacing to cover the gap
Stay silent until you remember the word
quiz.explain: Silence should be used instead of vocalized pauses or fillers when thinking.

quiz.q: Why should you include a pause immediately after delivering a key piece of information?
options: To create a moment of suspense
To give the audience time to absorb the information
To signal that you have finished the entire presentation
quiz.explain: Pausing after a point helps the audience process and digest the information.

examples.student: My research covers three main areas. But the most critical finding... [pause] ...is that the current model is fundamentally flawed. [pause] This changes how we view the entire dataset.
examples.job_seeker: I have a decade of experience in sales. However, my greatest strength... [pause] ...is my ability to listen to what the client isn't saying. [pause] That is how I close the deal.
examples.customer_facing: I understand this delay is frustrating. Here is the solution... [pause] ...I am going to personally oversee your order until it arrives. [pause] You have my word.
examples.creator: Everyone thinks success is about luck. But the truth... [pause] ...is that it's about showing up when you're terrified. [pause] Let me show you why.
examples.everyday: I know you really want me to come to the party. But... [pause] ...I need to prioritize my mental health this weekend. [pause] I hope you understand.
examples.new_here: Adjusting to this city has been a challenge. But the most important thing I've learned... [pause] ...is that kindness is a universal language. [pause] It makes every difference.

student.setup: You are presenting your final research findings during a one-on-one review.
student.opening: You've given me a lot of data today. If there is just one key takeaway you want me to remember, what is it?

job_seeker.setup: You are at the end of a high-stakes interview for a leadership role.
job_seeker.opening: We have a few great candidates. Before you go, what is the one thing you want me to remember about you?

customer_facing.setup: A shipment was lost, and you are calling the client to resolve the conflict.
customer_facing.opening: I'm tired of excuses. Just tell me the one thing I should remember about how you're fixing this.

creator.setup: You are pitching a new video series concept to a producer.
creator.opening: Your portfolio is impressive, but this project is huge. What's the one core message you want the viewers to remember?

everyday.setup: You are trying to set a boundary regarding your free time.
everyday.opening: Come on, just one night! If you're really saying no, what's the one reason you want me to remember?

new_here.setup: You are sharing your experience of moving to the country during a coffee break.
new_here.opening: It must have been a whirlwind move. Looking back, what's the one thing you want me to remember about your journey?

rubric.check: Has one clear key line or message that stands out
The transcript shows a pause around the key line (a pause marker [pause] next to it)
Uses silence instead of filler words (um, uh, like) around the key line
